Naive: media through the API and a fan-out-on-read feed. Both break at this scale.
Media: the client uploads directly to S3 with a presigned URL; an S3 event triggers thumbnails and renditions; the CDN serves them.

items: Media: the client uploads directly to S3 with a presigned URL; an S3 event triggers thumbnails and renditions; the CDN serves them.
Feed: same as News Feed. New posts go to Kafka, workers push post IDs into followers' Redis feeds, and celebrities are pulled at read time (hybrid).
Post visible before media is processed?
Keep status PROCESSING; show it once renditions are ready (or show to the author only).
Celebrities?
Hybrid fan-out as in News Feed.
Like counts?
Redis INCR or sharded counters, flushed asynchronously to the DB.
Global latency?
CDN for media; regional read replicas or caches for the feed.
Serving images from app servers or storing blobs in the database.
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
Ignoring retries, timeouts and crashes.
